summary: Specifies an IPv6 Router Advertisement option so routers can tell hosts the addresses of recursive DNS servers. It is experimental and was replaced by RFC 6106.

eli5.summary: A router tells every new device where the internet's phone book helper is. A newer RFC replaced this.

questions: how do ipv6 hosts learn dns servers
can router advertisements carry dns information
how does ipv6 dns configuration work
subtitle: Routers advertise DNS server addresses alongside IPv6 network configuration.

tldr.problem: IPv6 hosts need to know the addresses of DNS servers to look up domain names, but getting this information requires either manual configuration or a separate DHCP exchange. For mobile hosts using stateless address autoconfiguration, DHCP adds delay and complexity.
tldr.mechanism: A new Router Advertisement option (RDNSS) carries the IPv6 addresses of recursive DNS servers. Hosts learn DNS server addresses from the same Router Advertisement that configures their network, with no additional protocol run.
tldr.outcome: Hosts on mobile networks and wireless LANs can acquire local DNS servers faster and without extra overhead. The approach was experimental; RFC 6106 provides the standard-track version.

today: RFC 5006 is Experimental. It was superseded by RFC 6106, which provides the standard-track specification for the RDNSS option with clarifications and additional guidance.

sections.title: DNS Configuration and Neighbor Discovery
sections.content:
IPv6 hosts configure their network addresses and default routers through Neighbor Discovery (ND) Router Advertisements, which arrive automatically from routers on the link. However, learning the addresses of recursive DNS servers has no equivalent automatic mechanism in IPv6 Neighbor Discovery.

RFC 5006 defines a new Router Advertisement option called RDNSS (Recursive DNS Server) that carries DNS server addresses. This allows routers to advertise DNS servers at the same time they advertise network configuration. For mobile hosts and nomadic devices (like laptops switching between wireless networks), avoiding an additional DHCP exchange saves time and is particularly valuable in Mobile IPv6 scenarios where address acquisition delays matter.
sections.eli5: When a router says 'here is your new network address,' it can also say 'and here are the phone book helpers you should use.' This saves time, especially for traveling computers.

sections.title: The RDNSS Router Advertisement Option
sections.content:
The RDNSS option has a type value of 25 assigned by IANA. It includes a 32-bit lifetime field indicating how long the DNS server addresses are valid, and one or more 128-bit IPv6 addresses of recursive DNS servers. All addresses in a single RDNSS option share the same lifetime.

The option is carried in Router Advertisement messages, either unsolicited (sent periodically by the router) or solicited (sent in response to a Router Solicitation). A router can send multiple RDNSS options if it wishes to advertise servers with different lifetimes. The length field determines how many addresses are present: length is 3 for one address, and increases by 2 for each additional address.
sections.eli5: The option is a small label in the router's announcement that says 'DNS servers at 2001:db8::1 and 2001:db8::2 are good for the next 3600 seconds.'

sections.title: Host Processing and Lifetime Management
sections.content:
When an IPv6 host receives a Router Advertisement with one or more RDNSS options, it extracts the addresses and stores them in two places: a DNS Server List (maintained by the network stack kernel or process) and a Resolver Repository (the host's DNS configuration, like /etc/resolv.conf on Unix). The host respects the lifetime field: servers are used only while their lifetime has not expired.

The lifetime SHOULD be set to a value between the router's MaxRtrAdvInterval and twice that interval, providing stability for fixed hosts while allowing mobile hosts to prefer recently announced, local DNS servers. A lifetime of zero means the server is no longer valid and should be removed. A lifetime of all ones (0xffffffff) means infinity.

Hosts manage the server list by updating expiration times when new advertisements arrive for the same server, and removing expired entries. An RDNSS address is valid only if both the router's lifetime and the RDNSS option's lifetime have not expired.
sections.eli5: The host keeps a list of which DNS servers work, along with when they expire. When the router announces new servers or updates, the list is refreshed. Dead entries are thrown away when their time runs out.

sections.title: Implementation Considerations
sections.content:
Implementations may process ND in the kernel while the DNS resolver library runs in user space. Synchronizing the kernel's DNS Server List with the user-space Resolver Repository requires careful coordination. A common approach is a daemon that monitors the lifetimes of kernel-side DNS entries and updates the resolver configuration when entries expire.

Hosts may ignore additional DNS servers beyond a reasonable limit (for example, keeping only the first three). An RDNSS address MUST only be used if the advertising router itself is still reachable (the router lifetime has not expired), ensuring that stale server advertisements from dead routers are not used.
sections.eli5: The operating system's network layer and the DNS library need to agree on which servers are valid. A helper program watches for expiring servers and keeps them in sync.

sections.title: Security and Deployment
sections.content:
The security of the RDNSS option is similar to that of Router Advertisements in general. A malicious host on the LAN can send unsolicited RAs with false DNS server addresses, potentially redirecting name lookups. This is not a new vulnerability; any node on a LAN can already perform similar attacks through other means.

If the Secure Neighbor Discovery (SEND) protocol is in use, RDNSS options are included in SEND signatures, protecting their integrity. However, SEND cannot authorize which hosts may send RDNSS options, only that they have been signed. Site administrators should consider administratively disabling RA-based DNS configuration on routers and clients if such attacks are a concern, and can instead rely on DHCPv6 for DNS server discovery.
sections.eli5: A bad actor on your network could lie about DNS servers, like any other router attack. If you use SEND (a signing system for router ads), at least you know they were not tampered with. You can turn off RA-based DNS if you do not trust your LAN.

fields.name: Length
fields.desc: Length in units of 8 octets; minimum 3 for one address.

fields.name: Lifetime
fields.desc: Maximum time in seconds this RDNSS address may be used. 0xffffffff = infinity.

fields.name: Addresses
fields.desc: One or more IPv6 addresses of recursive DNS servers. Additional addresses continue beyond this example.
